Dear Bruce

Following is a brief update on the RTX phase 1 status:

1. The power source for the electronics has been changed from (2) 3 volt Lithium batteries BR 1225 to (4) 1.5 volt Silver Oxide batteries D369/390B by DURACELL. Based on our breadboard testing and calculations, assuming 480 puffs per day, these batteries are estimated to last 15 to 30 days.

2. The enclosure design has been changed to accommodate (4) batteries (button cells) with a separate access door.

3. To protect against excessive FET die temperature in case of a shorted load resistor, we have incorporated a 6 Amp current fuse. The fuse is a 8MD nano fuse from LITTLE FUSE and will be soldered directly to the flex circuit. In order for the fuse to open at least one load resistor must be shorted and the FET driving the shorted load resistor must be turned on.

The above changes had an impact on the design, the tools and fabrication of the three housing parts; bottom, top and battery cover.
The flex circuit had to be changed to accommodate the fuse, the battery change and some circuit revisions as a result of the breadboard testing.

We were able to incorporate all changes without a major impact on the schedule.
Today we have received the first tooled housing parts based on the latest design.
The first PRT substrate assembly has been built and tested. The flex circuit design is completed and will be released for fabrication week of 9/3. The fabrication time of the flex circuit will determine when we can deliver the first modules to you. Our best estimate at this time is late Sep. I will call you on 9/7 with the latest estimate.
